text:
frank: heads-up: after the docusaurus rollout i'm seeing ambiguous fragment jumps on /examples/compose. The TOC links to `#compose-examples` but there are two headings that resolve to that slug (one is `Compose examples (v1)` and the other `Compose examples - v2`). In prod the anchor jumps to whichever HTML id appears first.

anya: saw that in the nightly linkcheck. linkcheck reported a present fragment but users reported it goes to the wrong example. We should avoid duplicate slugs across one page.

frank: quick repro: build the site (`yarn build`) and open `build/examples/compose/index.html`  you'll see both `<h2 id=\"compose-examples\">` entries. Docusaurus slugifier collapsed the parentheses and hyphen the same way.

-dev-bot: buildkite/docs-validate #1239 failed: ambiguous fragment `/examples/compose#compose-examples` flagged by UX test (found 2 elements with id=compose-examples).

sophie: two fixes: 1) give explicit ids to headings (e.g. `{#compose-examples-v1}` and `{#compose-examples-v2}`) and update internal TOC links; 2) add a docs CI check that detects duplicate ids in the built HTML and fails the PR to prevent regressions.

anya: i'll take the PR to normalize ids and update the TOC. small preference: keep ids ASCII kebab-case and stable (no auto appended -1) so external links stay consistent.

frank: pushed branch `docs/compose-anchors` with the changes. also added a script `scripts/check_duplicate_ids.sh` that runs after build and greps for duplicate id attributes: 
```bash
# run after yarn build
grep -o 'id=\"[^\"]\\+' -h build/**/*.html | sort | uniq -d
```
this returns duplicates so CI can fail fast.

-dev-bot: buildkite/docs-validate #1241 started (includes duplicate-id check).

anya: small nit: for long pages with multiple sections we should prefer scoped ids that include the section path, e.g. `{#compose-v1-examples}`. This reduces chance of collision across pages or if headings are programatically concatenated.

sophie: agreed. also adding a note to the contributor guide: "When adding headings that may be repeated (versions, examples, steps), use full-scope explicit ids: `{#<page>-<section>-<qualifier>}`." Example table added to the styleguide PR.

frank: CI failure log shows another oddity: some markdown-generated admonitions also had ids that matched headings (admonition titles slugify to the same value). i've added a small mdx transform in the PR that strips implied ids from admonition wrappers so they won't collide.

-dev-bot: buildkite/docs-validate #1241 failed: duplicate id `compose-examples` still present in interim artifacts (pre-transform).

anya: pushed fix: run the admonition id-stripping transform earlier in the pipeline and re-run the duplicate-id check against the final build dir. local `yarn build && ./scripts/check_duplicate_ids.sh` returns nothing now. Marking PR ready.

-dev-bot: buildkite/docs-validate #1243 succeeded: duplicate-id check passed, linkcheck passed.

frank: merged PR at 1819994375. Leaving release-note suggestion: "docs: disambiguate repeated example headings by introducing scoped explicit header ids; add duplicate-id check to docs CI; strip generated ids from admonition wrappers to avoid collisions."

sophie: follow-up: open a follow-up PR to add a lintrule that warns when a heading contains parentheses/emoji/backticks without an explicit id. The linter should point to the styleguide. That will catch most of the migration pain.

anya: also filing an issue to scan older pages for likely collisions (pattern: headings that share the same base slug). We can run `scripts/compute_slugs.py --scan docs/` and report top collisions.

-link-bot: buildkite/docs-scan #200 triggered: preliminary scan found 27 probable slug collisions across /examples and /tutorials.

frank: thanks everyone. we'll triage those in the next docs sprint. Closing this thread.
